newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea to sell 6.75 mln shares of Korea Telecom.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea to sell 6.75 mln shares of Korea Telecom.

text.p: The South Korean government plans to sell 6.75 million shares, valued at about 300 billion won, of state-backed Korea Telecom through a public auction on October 14, the Finance Ministry said in a statement on Wednesday.
The ministry said the auction represented 2.34 percent of the telephone service provider's total outstanding shares.
The minimum bid was set at 44,500 won per share. Twenty percent of the newly available stocks were reserved for Korea Telecom employees, the statement said.

Only domestic institutional investors and national pension funds will be eligible to bid for the shares. But securities houses, investment trust firms and specialised banks, such as the Korea Development Bank and the Korea Exchange Bank, will be prohibited from participating.
The ministry set a maximum purchase limit of 337,500 shares or five percent of the available stock.

Successful buyers cannot sell the Korea Telecom shares for six months after the listing on the Korea Stock Exchange. But the ministry did not say when Korea Telecom would begin trading publicly, although analysts believe it may do so next year.

The company has a monopoly on South Korea's local telephone service, and holds the lion's share of the long distance and data communications markets. The government currently holds about an 80 percent stake in Korea Telecom.
